No front door

"No DM advice", and no next step

Your bio rightly says no DM advice. But someone moved by a reel has nowhere in between to go: no class, no list, no gentle next step. Most of them take none.

Amazon owns the reader

Every book buyer is a stranger

When a reader buys your book on Amazon, the retailer gets their details, not you. Your most motivated readers can't hear from you again unless they come back on their own.

Content treadmill

2,219 posts and counting

Growth still leans on the next post, episode and interview. When you step back to write or rest, new enquiries step back too.

The people who love your content but aren't ready for 1:1 today have no clear next step with you, so most of them drift away.

My recommendation

A free masterclass that sells your book and fills your 1:1 sessions

You already have the audience, the authority and a book. What's missing is one free 60-minute class that teaches your approach to boundaries and family guilt, offers your book bundle on the thank-you page, and invites the right people to apply for 1:1. Meta ads then put that class in front of new people every day.

Fixes the missing front door

One free class becomes the link in your bio and the destination for your ads. Every sign-up is an email you own, and every attendee sees how you think before you ask for anything.

Fixes the missing qualifier

The replay page invites people who want 1:1 support to apply. You only talk to people who watched, stayed and told you what they want to change.

Turns readers into your list

Your book is offered at the moment people are most motivated, and sold from your own page, so every buyer becomes someone you can keep teaching. It helps pay for the ads.

The 95%*

Not ready for 1:1 yet

They join the free class, pick up your book bundle on the thank-you page, and keep learning from your emails and podcast. They pay you while they build trust.

The qualified 5%

Ready for 1:1 support

They watch to the end and apply on the replay page. The application filters for fit before your calendar, and three pre-call emails prepare them for the conversation.

*The 95% / 5% split is an industry estimate, not your data.

Two ways people tend to respond to a guilt trip. In my free class I teach the second one, step by step.

Two ways to answer a guilt trip

Explain and defendLong reasons, apologies, then giving in anyway. The same conversation happens again next month.
Short, calm, kindOne clear sentence, no over-explaining, and a plan for the pushback. Fewer repeat battles over time.

Static 3 · Contrast layout · Hook: two ways to answer a guilt trip

Script 1 · Reel · 30 to 45 seconds

"The holiday guilt question"

Hook
"Every year people ask me the same question before the holidays: do I have to go?" (to camera, outdoors, natural greenery behind, the same look as your profile photo)
Body
"What they're really asking is: am I allowed to choose? Most of us were handed a family script long before we could question it. Guilt is often that script talking, not your values. The skill is learning to tell the two apart." (simple on-screen captions)
CTA
"I teach exactly how in a free 60-minute class called Beyond the Family Script. Tap Sign up to save your seat. Educational content, not therapy."
Script 2 · Reel · 30 seconds

"One sentence, no essay"

Hook
"The biggest boundary mistake I see? Writing an essay when one sentence will do." (Dr. Sherrie holds up one finger)
Body
"The more people explain, the more there is to argue with. A boundary can be short, calm and kind: 'I won't be coming this year, and I hope it's a lovely day.' Then you plan for the pushback, instead of hoping it won't come." (caption the example sentence on screen)
CTA
"I walk through the full approach in my free masterclass. Link below."
Script 3 · Reel · 45 seconds

"Where to start with my work"

Hook
"People ask me whether to start with my books, my podcast or 1:1. Here's my honest answer." (walking, natural light)
Body
"If you're new here, don't pick yet. Come to my free class first. You'll learn how I think about family roles, guilt and boundaries, try a few of the scripts that week, and know which next step fits you."
CTA
"It's called Beyond the Family Script, it's free, and there's a replay if you can't make it live. Tap Sign up."

Why setting boundaries with family brings up so much guiltSwipe →

Many people can say no at work. With family, the same word feels impossible.

That's often the family script: roles and rules learned long before anyone could question them

Guilt and responsibility can feel the same. They aren't.

A boundary can be one sentence.Short. Calm. Kind. No essay required.

And a plan for the pushback, so you're not caught off guard
